tables.title: Table 1
tables.content:
Material Types Advantages Disadvantages Ref.
Conventional perovskite ferroelectric materials ✓ High polarization value ✓ High commercialization value ◆ Strong depolarization field ◆ Incompatible with semiconductor devices ◆ Fatigue issue [7, 46]
Hafnium-based ferroelectric materials ✓ Ferroelectricity for one-unite cell ✓ High polarization value ✓ High dielectric constant and wide bandgap ✓ Compatible with semiconductor devices ◆ Metastable structure ◆ Large coercive field ◆ Fatigue issue [47]
2D intrinsic ferroelectric materials ✓ Ferroelectricity for monolayer ✓ Without dangling bonds ✓ Compatible with semiconductor devices ✓ Low power consumption ✓ High mobility ◆ Low polarization value ◆ Few 2D materials [48, 44, 49, 50]
Sliding ferroelectric materials ✓ Ferroelectricity for bilayer or multilayer ✓ Fatigue-free characteristics ✓ Without dangling bonds ✓ Compatible with semiconductor devices ✓ Low-power consumption ✓ More 2D materials ◆ Very low polarization value [1,2, 29, 33, 35]
